nodes.rationale: A timing context manager records a start timestamp in __enter__ and computes elapsed duration in __exit__ using time.monotonic() rather than time.time(), since a monotonic clock can't jump backward and corrupt the measurement.

nodes.label: importlib.metadata
nodes.rationale: importlib.metadata.version() reads installed package metadata without importing the package, enabling feature-detection; it raises PackageNotFoundError for missing packages, which callers should catch rather than crash on.

nodes.label: Lock Files
nodes.rationale: A lock file records the exact version actually installed rather than an acceptable range, so re-installing later or on another machine resolves to the identical version; a resolver that ignores the pin defeats that reproducibility guarantee.

nodes.label: requirements.txt
nodes.rationale: requirements.txt pins have a simple, predictable 'name==version' shape that can be parsed with str.partition on the first '==' rather than pulling in a full parser dependency.

nodes.label: Virtual Environments
nodes.rationale: sys.prefix differs from sys.base_prefix exactly when a virtualenv is active; comparing them is the standard, dependency-free venv-detection check used internally by pip and other tools.

nodes.label: Function Composition
nodes.rationale: compose(f, g) builds a new function equivalent to calling g first and passing its result to f, letting complex behavior be built from small, independently-testable pieces instead of one large function.

nodes.label: Partial Application
nodes.rationale: functools.partial(func, **fixed_kwargs) returns a new callable with some arguments already bound, expressing 'the same function with this argument fixed' more directly than a one-off wrapper lambda.

nodes.label: Pure Functions
nodes.rationale: A pure function's only effect is its return value; quietly mutating shared/module-level state on the side makes a function harder to test and reason about since its behavior depends on state outside its arguments.

nodes.label: contextvars
nodes.rationale: contextvars.ContextVar holds a value implicitly available anywhere in the same logical call chain (correctly isolated per-task under asyncio), avoiding the need to thread an explicit parameter like a correlation/request ID through every function signature.

nodes.label: Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: Required config read via os.environ[name] crashes with KeyError when unset; os.environ.get(name, default) degrades gracefully, and the string result must be explicitly converted to the needed type.

nodes.label: Graceful Shutdown
nodes.rationale: A deployed process typically receives SIGTERM on stop; the standard pattern registers a signal.signal() handler that flips a flag for the main loop to notice and wind down cleanly instead of being killed mid-request.

nodes.label: Health Checks
nodes.rationale: A readiness/liveness check exists to reflect whether a process's actual dependencies are healthy; a check that always reports 'ok' defeats its purpose because it can never catch a real outage.

nodes.label: Idempotency
nodes.rationale: Deploy steps get re-run (retries, re-applied deploys, config re-sync); a step that checks whether a resource already exists before acting can be re-run safely without duplicate work or misleading logs.

nodes.label: Metrics
nodes.rationale: Most real metrics systems (Prometheus counters, StatsD) reduce to a name mapping to a monotonically increasing number, incremented once per occurrence of the thing being measured.
